text: Among the Horizon 2020 projects whose EU science-vocabulary (euroSciVoc) classification includes superconductivity and that received EU funding above the 95th percentile of all H2020 projects (about EUR 6.93 million in EC contribution), how do they differ in the application domain they target and in the way they make use of superconductivity?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT p.id, p.acronym, ROUND(p.ecMaxContribution) AS ec FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID=p.id WHERE e.euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/superconductivity%' AND p.ecMaxContribution > 6926372.79 GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 3 DESC

reference_answer: All four are top-funded superconductivity projects but target sharply different domains. EcoSwing delivered the world's first demonstration of a high-temperature superconducting (HTS) direct-drive generator on a 3.6 MW wind turbine, using second-generation (2G) HTS wire coils to cut generator weight and rare-earth reliance in wind power. ARIES is a pan-European accelerator-infrastructure network that develops superconducting magnets, RF cavities with superconducting thin-film coatings, and cryogenics for particle accelerators and high-energy physics. NONLOCAL pursues fundamental quantum physics, engineering topological superconductivity and Majorana bound states in superconductor-semiconductor hybrid devices toward future quantum technologies, while HERO is a condensed-matter physics project searching for new hidden, entangled and resonating orders in correlated-electron quantum matter, where superconductivity figures as one example of the many-body paradigm rather than an engineered device.
notes: FILTER: P95 of project.ecMaxContribution over all 35,389 projects = 6926372.79 (re-executed this session via PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ecMaxContribution)). Superconductivity subtree matched with euroSciVocPath LIKE '%/superconductivity%' (paths carry no leading slash, per schema value note); subtree = 219 distinct projects; above-P95 survivors = exactly 4. text: An EU fellowship set out to make simulations of the chemistry of heavy elements affordable, because the electrons there move fast enough that Einstein's corrections matter. What did that project report about how those corrections change the average distance between one electron and another?
reference_answer: The project is ReReDMFT (891647), which extended Reduced Density Matrix Functional Theory to cover relativistic effects so that compounds of heavy elements could be simulated at an affordable cost. Its study of relativistic effects on electronic pair densities, run with the DIRAC program, found that those effects shrink the mean inter-electronic distance - relativity brings the electrons closer together.

text: How do EU-funded projects approach tax evasion that operates through the links between firms - the companies a business buys from, sells to or shares owners with - rather than being the act of a single company on its own?
reference_answer: Two projects approach tax evasion as something produced inside business relationships rather than by one firm acting alone. DEVTAXNET starts from the claim that the most common and hardest-to-detect forms of evasion involve interactions across firm networks, which earlier work missed because it had mostly considered taxpayers as isolated units; it sets out to study, using unique administrative datasets from Chile and Ecuador covering networks of supply chains and of joint ownership structures, profit shifting by multinational firms to low tax jurisdictions, profit shifting and tax collusion among firms within the same country, and how the tax compliance of local trading partners of foreign-owned firms is affected. AnthroTax takes the same idea into ethnographic fieldwork in Croatia, studying how practices of tax evasion play out between family winemakers in Istria and a massive agribusiness conglomerate with which they do business, and frames the arrangement as 'hostage barter', through which corporate tax evasion is enacted as an apparent 'natural' feature of everyday business in a predatory economy. In both, the trading relationship itself is the unit of analysis - approached through firm-to-firm transaction data in one case and through the weaker partner's experience in the other.

text: Which projects are developing chips or other dedicated hardware in which artificial neurons compute by firing brief pulses at each other, the way nerve cells do?
reference_answer: A cluster of H2020 projects builds computing hardware in which the signals are neuron-like pulses rather than clocked digital arithmetic. NeuRAM3 proposed to fabricate a chip implementing a neuromorphic architecture supporting spike-based learning, in FDSOI at 28nm design rules with RRAM synapses; MeM-Scales works on analog spiking microprocessors whose memory devices cover timescales spanning up to 9 orders of magnitude; SYNCH couples the brain of a living animal to a silicon neural network of spiking neurons on a chip through neuromorphic synapses; ULPEC connects a neuromorphic event-based camera to a Spiking Neural Network with memristive synapses; ChipAI builds resonant-tunnelling nanophotonic sources and detectors that fire and detect neuron-like light-spiking signals at >10 GHz per spike rates; NEPSpiNN puts event-based spiking processing of surface EMG into a compact ultra-low power neuromorphic chip; BeFerroSynaptic packaged TEXEL, a 9mm x 9mm neuromorphic chip carrying 180 adaptive-exponential integrate and fire (AdExp-I&F) neurons fed by ferroelectric synaptic devices; and TEMPO and ANDANTE develop the underlying technology and hardware platforms (integrate-and-fire engines, emerging memories, 3D integration, edge SNN chips). The same set also includes NANOINFER, whose intelligent memory chips combine digital CMOS logic with spiking neurons circuits, Fun-COMP, whose nanoelectronic and nanophotonic building blocks implement spiking neural networks in hardware, NeuroAgents, which fabricated the DYNAP-SE2 mixed-signal Spiking Neuronal Network processor for neuromorphic robotic agents, and SOFT, which designed, fabricated and tested a magnetic domain-wall spiking neuron and used a magnetic neural network to recognise patterns from human voice converted into spikes.
notes:
SEEDS/GROUNDING: from corpus-profile candidate vector-60 (spiking hardware). Candidate evidence SQL re-executed this pass: SELECT p.id,p.acronym FROM project p WHERE p.objective ILIKE '%spiking neural%' OR p.objective ILIKE '%spiking neuron%' OR p.title ILIKE '%spiking%' -> 17 rows, identical id list to the candidate (no drift). Objectives read in full for 687299, 705957, 707373, 715872, 724295, 732642, 747848, 753470, 780848, 794425, 824162, 826655, 828841, 871371, 871501, 876925, 658479, 705100, 773228, 788793, 694829, 695459, 713736, 785911, 871330, 888129, 956601, 101016734.
GOLD CRITERION (positive, applied evenly): the project's own work delivers physical computing hardware - a chip, integrated circuit, photonic or other fabricated device - in which the computation itself is carried by spikes/pulses fired between artificial (silicon, photonic, magnetic) neurons. Three consequences, applied to every project alike: (a) projects that model or simulate spiking neurons in software, or study spiking in biological tissue, are OUT; (b) neuromorphic/analog/in-memory hardware whose computation is not carried by neuron pulses (memristive or ferroelectric synapse materials on their own, oscillatory or reservoir computing, in-memory matrix multiplication) is OUT; (c) a project is OUT when the spiking computation it reports was run on neuromorphic hardware it did not itself deliver - whether the vehicle is a named external platform (ROLLS, Dynap-se, SCAMP, SpiNNaker) or an unnamed 'programmable neuromorphic substrate' - because in every such case the project's own deliverable is an algorithm, model, architecture or readout circuit rather than the spiking device. 707373 ECogNeT, 794425 STRoNA and 747848 ProbSenS are all excluded on this single ground.

text: What do EU-funded projects on cancer cachexia identify as the drivers of the wasting of adipose tissue and muscle in cancer patients?
reference_answer: Two projects study cancer cachexia head-on and together describe it as a whole-body failure rather than a muscle-local one. CSI-Fun treats cancer associated cachexia (CAC) as a disorder of the whole body affecting 50-80% of cancer patients and the immediate cause of death for a third of them, and demonstrated experimentally that uncontrolled inflammation and the beta-adrenergic system are important players, with immune cells interacting with the sympathetic nervous system during CAC. StopWaste locates the driver in metabolism: its data support the concept that tumours activate futile substrate cycling in adipocytes, and the project identified cachexia-specific bioreactive lipids stemming from altered liver lipids and dysregulated liver lipid enzymes, which could be targeted with the ceramide synthesis inhibitor myriocin, plus an altered flux of fatty acids and amino acids through the tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA) in cachectic adipose tissue, partly linked to the TCA gatekeeper PDK4. Combining them, the wasting of fat and muscle is driven by inflammation and neuro-endocrine signalling acting on a reprogrammed lipid and glucose metabolism spanning tumour, adipose tissue and liver, with disturbed glucose metabolism appearing early - patients with disturbed glucose metabolism showed a higher incidence of cachexia associated with pancreatic and colorectal cancers.

text: Which projects are engineering CAR T cells to attack solid tumours?
reference_answer: Eight H2020 projects engineer chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells against solid tumours, the setting where CAR therapy has lagged behind its success in blood cancers. Several build new CAR specificities: AngioCAR aims CAR T cells at extracellular vimentin (eVim) on the tumour vasculature, SweetCAR at sialic-acid carbohydrate neoantigens on carcinomas, and CARsen at senescent cells in solid tumours and senescence-associated disease. Others attack the hostile tumour microenvironment instead - Exh-Res-CART and Tex-Mex both work on T-cell exhaustion (biochemical and biomechanical triggers respectively), TRAP-CART uses gene-modified blood-derived cells in the tumour microenvironment to switch on programmable CAR T cells locally, with melanoma as its model cancer, and EnhancemenT modulates ZFP36/ZFP36L1 RNA-binding proteins in CAR-T cells to raise their in-vivo solid tumour-fighting capacity. CARAT is the platform case: automated GMP-compliant manufacture of CAR-modified T cells together with innovative CAR designs, intended to serve patients with incurable solid tumours as well as haematologic malignancies.

text: Which project set out to backhaul dense 5G small cells by exploiting the millimetre wave spectrum above 100 GHz, combining D-band point-to-multipoint coverage with G-band point-to-point feeder links and using newly designed traveling wave tubes to provide the transmission power?
reference_answer: ULTRAWAVE. text: How is European research trying to replace the traditional remedy for people bitten by poisonous snakes - the kind produced from the blood of animals repeatedly exposed to the poison - with proteins engineered in the laboratory instead?
reference_answer: Two projects pursue laboratory-made replacements for conventional antivenoms, which are derived from immunised animals (ADDovenom notes current products come from hyperimmunised horses and sheep, that only 10-15% of their IgGs bind venom, and that repeat vials raise adverse effects and cost). MABSTER used phage display selections together with synthetic biology and antibody/antigen engineering to find recombinant human monoclonal antibodies that are recyclable (able to neutralise more than one snake toxin per antibody) and broadly neutralising across similar toxins from several species; it developed and patented a universal pH-switch for antibodies, which resulted in the spinout Y-king Biologics and EUR 3 million in secured funding, and it also contributed nanobodies and computationally designed minibinders against snake toxins, published in Nature Communications and Nature. ADDovenom builds a fully synthetic platform instead, generating neutralising ADDobodies and ADDomer particles - plus nanobodies - against pathogenic snake toxins, and has shown neutralisation of recombinant PLA2 toxins and of whole venom, with Sub-Saharan Africa as the target setting in line with the WHO goal of halving snakebite mortality and morbidity by 2030. Together they show two complementary engineering routes to the same goal: re-engineering human antibody formats on one side, and a designed protein scaffold carrying many binding sites on the other.

text: Among the Marie Sklodowska-Curie individual fellowships classified under cognitive neuroscience and hosted by an organisation in the Netherlands, how do the ones that act on the brain from outside the head, rather than only measuring it, use that to test whether a particular brain area or the pace of its activity is genuinely doing the work?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM project p JOIN euroscivoc e ON e.projectID = p.id JOIN organization o ON o.projectID = p.id WHERE p.fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%' AND e.euroSciVocTitle = 'cognitive neuroscience' AND o.role = 'coordinator' AND o.country = 'NL' ORDER BY p.id

reference_answer: Three of these fellowships intervene rather than only observe, and they split by direction. ORCA drives activity with transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS), synchronising rhythmic activity between two attention-related regions while recording EEG and, in a second study, fMRI; it found no effect on spatial attention in 23 participants but a frequency-specific effect on vigilant attention in 101 participants, which it reads as the first causal evidence for the medial frontal cortex in vigilant attention. NERHYMUS and MemoryBasedPercepts instead damp a named region with transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) and ask whether performance suffers: NERHYMUS uses neuronavigated TMS combined with EEG to down-regulate the supplementary motor area (SMA) and test whether that region is really necessary for processing rhythm in speech, and a preliminary analysis of 9 non-musician datasets suggests the TMS does affect processing of regular rhythm in poems. MemoryBasedPercepts first characterises memory-based percepts with fMRI and MEG and then applies TMS to test whether activity of visual cortex is causally necessary for them, reporting that it is - those visual regions are directly implicated in producing knowledge-driven perception.
notes:
FILTER RATIONALE. Three predicates, every one a stored column and every one stated in the question: p.fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%' (the MSCA individual-fellowship family, which includes MSCA-IF, MSCA-IF-EF-ST and MSCA-IF-GF), e.euroSciVocTitle = 'cognitive neuroscience', and a Dutch coordinator. 17 survivors - inside filter-synthesize's 5-20 window and far under the 200-row enumerability ceiling. Intermediate counts re-executed this pass: MSCA-IF x cognitive neuroscience = 108 before the country predicate; MSCA-IF x NL coordinator = 625 without the leaf.

ONE-READING CHECK. euroSciVocPath ILIKE '%cognitive neuroscience%' returns exactly ONE row - path 'natural sciences/biological sciences/neurobiology/cognitive neuroscience', 201 projects corpus-wide - so the title reading and the subtree reading select the identical set and the scope has one executable reading.

WORDING ROBUSTNESS. 'hosted by an organisation in the Netherlands' cannot be read two ways here: the coordinator reading (role='coordinator' AND country='NL') and the any-participant reading (country='NL', any role) both return the identical 17 ids - EXCEPT in both directions returns 0 rows. The recorded SQL uses the coordinator reading.

ADJUDICATION - EXHAUSTIVE. S=17 <= 20, so every survivor was read and adjudicated this pass; no pooling gap exists. The three IN projects were read at full payload (objective + all report sections); the OUTs from objective/teaser.
IN 702402 ORCA - applies transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) to synchronise rhythmic activity between two attention regions, explicitly to 'investigate the causal role of neural oscillations in attention'; reports a frequency-specific effect on vigilant attention and a causal role for medial frontal cortex.
IN 794455 NERHYMUS - 'will employ transcranial brain stimulation (TMS) to disrupt pre-SMA involvement in rhythm perception in order to examine whether this region is really necessary'; report confirms neuronavigated TMS, combined EEG-TMS, and a preliminary SMA effect on regular rhythm in poems.
IN 101033489 MemoryBasedPercepts - 'I will use Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) to test whether activity of visual cortex is causally necessary'; report confirms the stimulation was run and the necessity established.
OUT 657255 NeWMaBIL - MEG only; measures oscillatory correlates of working-memory control in aged bilinguals, no intervention.
OUT 703493 NEUROBUKIMI - fMRI of emotional responses to virtual characters plus a questionnaire; observational.
OUT 704992 CraNOC - does perturb causally, but with viral optogenetic tools controlling the nucleo-olivary pathway inside the animal brain; not from outside the head.
OUT 705010 Detect and React - event-related potentials plus a driving simulator; measures detection and reaction, never acts on the brain.
OUT 706714 CONNECT - multi-modal molecular and magnetic neuroimaging of amyloid/tau/activity interaction; observational.
OUT 707727 AVISSO - EEG and fMRI, and it does test necessity, but by studying Parkinson's patients with dysfunctional basal ganglia; a patient-group design, not an applied intervention.
OUT 707865 Expectancy learning - EEG, MRI and Bayesian modelling of expectancy formation; observational.
OUT 791181 SOURCES - fMRI, EEG and eye-tracking on arousal and decision strategies; observational.
OUT 800046 NeuroPred - Event-Related Optical Signal, eye-tracking and MEG; observational.
OUT 841909 FromObjectsToScenes - fMRI and MEG on object-constellation processing; observational.
OUT 843379 ResonanceCircuits - does perturb causally, but by optogenetically silencing GABAergic interneuron classes with implanted laminar probes in awake mice; the flickering light is a sensory stimulus, not an action on the brain, so it fails 'from outside the head'.
OUT 844734 ToMComputations - two fMRI experiments on Theory of Mind; observational.
OUT 101025627 MyeSync - subcellular patch-clamp, Ca2+ imaging and in vivo electrophysiology in animals; invasive recording, no transcranial intervention.
OUT 101030415 ReWoMeN - mathematical and deep-neural-network modelling of working-memory recall; no experiment on a brain at all.

BORDERLINES, STATED. 704992 CraNOC and 843379 ResonanceCircuits both intervene causally and would be IN under a looser reading ('perturb the brain'); they are OUT because the question says 'from outside the head', and optogenetics needs virus and implanted hardware. 707727 AVISSO tests necessity but by choosing a patient group rather than by acting on a brain. These three are the question's real discriminators and a reader has to resolve them from the text.

NON-EMBEDDING SWEEP. Over the 17 survivors' concatenated objective + report teaser/summary/workPerformed/finalResults, ILIKE on transcranial / TMS / tACS / brain stimulation / stimulat%. Six survivors matched anything; only 702402, 794455 and 101033489 matched a transcranial term. 843379 matched via 'stimuli' and 'optogenetic', 707865 and 791181 via 'stimulus/stimuli' only. The sweep found nothing the exhaustive read had missed.

FILTER LOAD-BEARING - three independent lines. (1) Unscoped pooled search on the final question text returned 25 distinct projects and NOT ONE of them is a survivor: with the filter dropped, retrieval does not reach the gold set at all. (2) SQL counter-example count: 132 projects corpus-wide name TMS or tACS in their objective; 129 fall outside the filter and exactly 3 fall inside - the 3 gold. (3) Named counter-examples, each read this pass and each failing exactly ONE conjunct: 725970 NATVIS (NL coordinator, has the cognitive neuroscience leaf, but ERC-COG) uses 'fMRI, MEG, and TMS' and tests 'causal interactions between scene- and object-selective pathways in visual cortex' - fails only fundingScheme; 799238 BetweenTwoBrains (MSCA-IF, has the leaf, UK coordinator) uses 'dual transcranial alternating current stimulation (dual-tACS)' to 'test the hypothesis that there is a causal link' - fails only country; 798619 TUNING-BRAKES (MSCA-IF, NL coordinator, no cognitive neuroscience leaf) is entirely about tACS as a 'non-invasive brain stimulation technique' probing 'the causal role of interactions between beta oscillations' - fails only the leaf. So every conjunct of the filter is individually load-bearing, not merely the filter as a whole.

TEXT LOAD-BEARING. No stored column records what method a project uses. The filter alone hands back 17 projects with nothing to separate them; which three act on the brain, what they target and what they concluded exists only in objective and report free text.

TERM_STYLE = paraphrase.
